title: Solve a sliding number puzzle
instruction: Slide adjacent numbered tiles into the empty space in the fixed tray until the rows read 1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 blank. Keep the tiles flat in the tray and release them when finished.
context: A robot solves a tabletop educational puzzle used for play and spatial reasoning. The task combines planning around one empty cell with precise gripper access between neighboring tiles.
setup: Dual YAM arms and three calibrated cameras. A fixed 236 x 236 mm plastic tray holds eight 55 g plastic tiles on a 72 mm grid. Each tile has a 70 x 70 x 7 mm foot, a 42 x 42 mm face and 27 mm total height, leaving a recessed rim. Initial rows: 1 2 3 / 5 blank 6 / 4 7 8. Tray center: x=0.30 m, y=-0.04 m on the table.
scoring: Final state only: 1 if the rows are 123 / 456 / 78 blank; otherwise 0. Seven tile centers must be within 3 mm of their targets; one may be within 10 mm. Tiles must be seated (base height within 1 mm), correctly oriented (within 10 degrees) and released (robot contact below 0.05 N). No partial credit.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 simulation seconds), including the observation preroll and final settling.
reset_notes: Fixed initial layout, seed 0, no random jitter. Reload the scene and settle for 2 seconds before starting the task clock.
fidelity: Isaac Sim 6.1 CPU PhysX TGS at 240 Hz. Fixed rigid tray; eight free rigid tiles with compound convex collision meshes and Coulomb friction. Native YAM actuators and 14-D joint-position/gripper actions for both policies. No tile drives or grasp attachments; plastic compliance is not modeled.
